clues.title: Vietnam drives on the right side of the road
text: Vietnam drives on the **right side** of the road.
NOTE: Cambodia and the Philippines are the only other southeast Asian countries with normal Street View that drives on the right side.

clues.title: Plate: Vietnamese licence plates are white with black lettering
text: Vietnamese licence plates are **white** with black lettering. Both long and short versions are in use.

clues.title: Language: The Vietnamese language uses a modified version of the…
text: The Vietnamese language uses a modified version of the Latin script, but with a far larger number of **diacritics** than any other script found on Street View. Words are generally somewhat short, typically consisting of a **single syllable**.

clues.title: Bollard: The most common bollard type is a small square concrete…
text: The most common bollard type is a small square concrete bollard that is painted **white with a red top**.

clues.title: Sign: The posts of road signs are usually painted with a red and…
text: The posts of road signs are usually painted with a **red and white stripe** pattern.

clues.title: Sign: Road signs have a yellow-orange background
text: Road signs have a **yellow-orange background**. Within southeast Asia, this is unique.

clues.title: Route marker: Waystones that are painted white with a colourful top
text: Waystones that are painted white with a **colourful top**, usually red or blue, are common throughout the country.

NOTE: Waystones like these are also common in Thailand and Cambodia. Often, they will include the road number in a large font on the side, and in a smaller font in the red area on the back and front. In addition, the front and back will list distances to towns. This information can be really helpful with pinpointing.

clues.title: Chevron: Chevrons are either black on yellow or white on red and…
text: Chevrons are either **black on yellow** or **white on red** and typically only have one arrow.

clues.title: Direction sign: Directional signs are typically blue with either a very…
text: Directional signs are typically blue with either a very [thin white border](https://maps.app.goo.gl/u7UCtnpyaBFKZ1bR6) or no border at all. The signs usually contain white arrows, which rather than being orthogonal often point in slightly strange directions.

clues.title: Road line: While multiple different types of road lines
text: While multiple different types of road lines, both white and yellow, can be found in Vietnam, unusually **short yellow middle dashes** are particularly common and distinct.

clues.title: Minor roads made of concrete blocks are very common in…
text: Minor roads made of **concrete blocks** are very common in Vietnam.
NOTE: This is also common in both the Philippines and Thailand, and to a lesser extent in Indonesia.

clues.title: Guardrail: Vietnam uses A-type guardrails
text: Vietnam uses A-type guardrails. Instead of having just one colour, each reflector is **red** on one side and **yellow** on the other, making them very recognisable.

clues.title: Guardrail: Red and white striped concrete safety barriers are somewhat…
text: Red and white striped concrete safety barriers are somewhat common on mountain roads.

clues.title: Pole: Holey poles, with holes either only on the lower half or…
text: **Holey poles**, with holes either only on the lower half or almost all the way to the top, are common in Vietnam.
NOTE: The only other Asian country that commonly has holey poles is Sri Lanka, where the holes are [significantly larger](https://maps.app.goo.gl/srBQjDH9RRz2uPG48).

clues.title: Pole: Vietnam often has round concrete poles with indents and…
text: Vietnam often has round concrete poles with indents and **small pin holes** near the top.
NOTE: The same type of pole is also common in [Cambodia](https://goo.gl/maps/JdVDH4F2dURiwAew8) as well as in [Taiwan](https://maps.app.goo.gl/pzPeYUqFoGAVftCb9).

clues.title: Pole: Poletops shaped like upside down trapezoids are common in…
text: Poletops shaped like **upside down trapezoids** are common in Vietnam.
NOTE: These may look similar to the poletops found in [central and northern Sulawesi](https://maps.app.goo.gl/F77f85pkPtnfWexk6), Indonesia.

clues.title: Pole: Double poles, which can be of different varieties, are…
text: Double poles, which can be of different varieties, are fairly common in Vietnam.

clues.title: Pole: Utility poles often feature these light grey electricity…
text: Utility poles often feature these light grey **electricity boxes**, which can have anywhere from 1 to 4 small indented windows. They have a very characteristic shape, where the bottom part** slopes down **slightly.

clues.title: Coverage: Vietnam has a fair amount of motorcycle coverage
text: Vietnam has a fair amount of **motorcycle coverage**. This can be recognized by the unique shape of the car blur, which vaguely resembles the shape of a bone, and extends slightly higher up on one side. Sometimes you will only see the [helmet of the motorcyclist](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Md2n5vSVD72w2y197).
There is both Generation 3 and [Generation 4](https://maps.app.goo.gl/C1gwqT4kMgTz54pE6) motorcycle coverage.
Vietnam has by far the most motorcycle coverage in the world. In particular, if you see this type of coverage in a rural place, you are almost guaranteed to be in Vietnam.

clues.title: Coverage: Shitcam can be found in some areas of Vietnam
text: **Shitcam** can be found in some areas of Vietnam. Notably, the shitcam coverage has a car blur similar to the one from the previous tip, which makes it distinct from other countries where shitcam usually has a larger and more circular blur.
NOTE: The areas in which shitcam can be found will be discussed further at the end of step 2.

clues.title: It is somewhat common to see grains being spread out on…
text: It is somewhat common to see grains being spread out on roads to dry.
NOTE: This practice is also common in the Philippines, and more rarely in Thailand as well.

clues.title: Sign: Addresses on signs are _extremely _common in Vietnam
text: **Addresses on signs** are _extremely _common in Vietnam, in particular on storefronts. These addresses follow a hierarchical sequence that usually goes from specific (house/building) to general (city/province). These can be tremendously helpful to find your exact location.
Usually an address will contain all or some of the following elements, from left to right:
- House and street number
- Ward/commune:
- - Ward (urban areas): **phường**
- - Commune (rural areas): **xã**
- District:
- - Urban district: **quận**
- - Rural district: **huyện**
- - District level town: **thị xã**
- - Municipal/provincial city:** thành phố**
- Province/City
- - Province: **tỉnh**
- - Municipality: **thành phố **(a municipality in Vietnam is a city that is on the same administrative level as a province, such as Ha Noi, or Hải Phòng)

These words are often abbreviated. For example, huyện can be abbreviated as just H., thành phố as just TP., etc. Additionally, sometimes the province itself may be abbreviated, for instance [here](https://maps.app.goo.gl/jrN2XEvhZ31gQmJy5) Thái Bình is abbreviated as TB.

clues.title: Coverage: The provinces are the most useful part of an address
text: The **provinces** are the most useful part of an address. They are easy to scan for on the map, but it is recommended to learn them by heart to find them even quicker on the map.
Often, the names of provinces are abbreviated. For example, Tien Giang is abbreviated TG. These can be especially useful to learn by heart to get an edge over your opponent.

It is important to note that Vietnam underwent an administrative reform in 2025, combining most provinces into larger ones and reducing the number of provinces significantly. This makes learning the (old) provinces by heart even more important: The overwhelming majority of coverage will be from before the reform, meaning that you cannot simply scan the map for some of the provinces’ names.
There are lots of resources available to learn the province names and abbreviations. We recommend [https://helloquiz.app/](https://helloquiz.app/).

clues.title: Area codes in Vietnam always start with a 2
text: **Area codes** in Vietnam always start with a 2, followed by one or two more digits, which are generally ordered from north to south.

clues.title: Plate: Vietnamese licence plate codes
text: Vietnamese licence plate codes, which are often painted onto the sides of trucks and other vehicles, are another useful clue to figure out the region.

clues.title: Some place name prefixes
text: Some place name prefixes, meaning the start of a city name, are regional within Vietnam.

clues.title: Wide open and completely flat agricultural fields are most…
text: Wide open and **completely flat agricultural fields** are most commonly seen in the Red River Delta and somewhat less commonly found in the Mekong River Delta.

clues.title: Vegetation: The Mekong Delta is an exceedingly flat
text: The Mekong Delta is an exceedingly flat, water-rich area. It is traversed by numerous very **straight canals**, often flanked by linear villages. It is one of the most densely populated parts of Vietnam, with cultivated fields essentially everywhere. The area is even more tropical than the rest of Vietnam, with lots of [palm trees](https://maps.app.goo.gl/EGM3APVzRnWeDun1A)** **and lush wetland vegetation.

clues.title: Landscape: The Central Highlands region tends to have a landscape with…
text: The **Central Highlands** region tends to have a landscape with a somewhat distinct vibe: often hilly with distant mountains, red soil, and often fairly dry, rolling agricultural fields. Additionally, the vegetation is a bit drier than in the rest of Vietnam (depending on the season).

clues.title: Vegetation: Rubber tree plantations are primarily found in the…
text: **Rubber tree plantations** are primarily found in the provinces to the north of Ho Chi Minh City, as well as in several parts of the Central Highlands.

Rubber trees can be recognized by their thin trunks. In Vietnam, it is typical for a section of the tree trunk to be wrapped in a piece of plastic. These trees tend to be neatly organized in a dense grid-like pattern.

clues.title: Tea plantations are primarily found in the north
text: **Tea plantations** are primarily found in the north, limited to several disconnected areas.
A major exception is the southern province of Lâm Đồng, which has a large tea area centred around the city of Bảo Lộc.
Tea plants can be recognized by their compact and neatly trimmed shape, with small dark green leaves. They are often, but not always, planted in windy rows on hillsides.

clues.title: Landscape: Clusters of Khasi pines growing on hills are very typical…
text: Clusters of [Khasi pines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_kesiya) growing on hills are very typical of far northeastern Vietnam, specifically the provinces of Lạng Sơn and Quảng Ninh.

clues.title: Dragonfruit farms are mostly found in two small areas in…
text: **Dragonfruit** farms are mostly found in two small areas in the south:
- around the city of Phan Thiết in Bình Thuận province
- a small area on the border between Long An and Tiền Giang, northeast of Mỹ Tho .
Dragonfruit resembles the end of an upturned wet mop.

clues.title: Landscape: The coastal region northeast of Phan Thiết city is…
text: The coastal region northeast of Phan Thiết city is noticeably **dry and sandy**, compared to the typical Vietnamese landscape. Some parts of this region are [very rocky](https://maps.app.goo.gl/6tocNAdH2VVzMKpv6) as well.

clues.title: Vegetation: Black pepper plantations are common in the area in and…
text: **Black pepper** plantations are common in the area in and around the Central highlands. Black pepper is a type of vine that is cultivated on tree trunks: the pepper plants shroud these trees with a dense cover of downward-pointing leaves, completely obscuring the tree’s trunk.

clues.title: Wind turbines can be found in a few clusters mainly in the…
text: Wind turbines can be found in a few clusters mainly in the southern half of the country.
Here are the clusters from most to least common:
- [Southeast of Dalat, near the coast](https://maps.app.goo.gl/C34Em7GXyZiXqygA6)
- [North of Buon Ma Thuot, Dak lak](https://maps.app.goo.gl/k7LRFPhiJeH7xBbg8)
- [South of Pleiku, Gia Lai](https://maps.app.goo.gl/2AhLumL2EKeHUUHv5)
- [Southeast of Dong Hoi, Quang Binh](https://maps.app.goo.gl/YruY1bs8FcDnyTqW8)
- [East of Quy Nhon, Binh Dinh](https://maps.app.goo.gl/PRERajWrQJeN9j6J7)
- [South of Ho Chi Minh City, offshore wind farms near the coast.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/pyei1AkN9WrmEcj8A)
- [Western Quang Tri province.](https://maps.app.goo.gl/1Ri5pFNTLLjdhLqy5)

clues.title: Architecture: Thin spires on the roofs of houses are almost exclusively…
text: Thin **spires on the roofs** of houses are almost exclusively found in the northern half of the country.

clues.title: Architecture: Houses in the Red River Delta
text: Houses in the Red River Delta (the flat, densely populated area around Hanoi) tend to have a **boxy** look, typically tall with **multiple storeys**. These houses often feature gaudy details that borrow heavily from antique Greco-Roman architecture: [pillars](https://maps.app.goo.gl/6ogDGMJHvMutZ46y9), [pediments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pediment), [classical-looking balconies](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9Z9mSB9wJCce7LXC7), etc.
Note that similar houses are sometimes found in the direct vicinity of Ho Chi Minh City.

clues.title: Architecture: Houses in the Mekong Delta also have a boxy
text: Houses in the Mekong Delta also have a boxy, concrete look, but are usually much less tall: they almost always consist of just a single, ground-level storey.

clues.title: Architecture: Traditional wooden houses are common in the northwest
text: **Traditional wooden houses** are common in the northwest. They commonly have one or several of the following features:
- Stilts holding up the house,
- corrugated metal roofs,
- triangular openings on the side of the roofs.

clues.title: Single graves in the middle of agricultural fields can be…
text: **Single graves** in the middle of agricultural fields can be found in the Red River Delta.

clues.title: Wooden fences made out of sticks
text: **Wooden fences** made out of sticks, or even bamboo, in a grid-like pattern, similar to fences commonly found in northeastern India, are found in the northern parts of Vietnam.

clues.title: Pole: Utility poles with large holes along most of the pole are…
text: Utility poles with **large holes** along most of the pole are common in northern Vietnam.

NOTE: Do not confuse this with the [regular holey pole](https://maps.app.goo.gl/xbMJe5paBUuoLzm2A), which is where the holes extend only halfway up the pole. This ½ of the holey pole is found throughout the entirety of Vietnam.

clues.title: Pole: Round concrete poles usually feature many pinholes on the…
text: Round concrete poles usually feature [many pinholes](https://maps.app.goo.gl/RfrXtSv9T5Vy5Smg6) on the top half of the pole, however in the north they often feature a minimal amount or even **no pinholes**.
NOTE: Although more rare, pinhole poles may be found in the north.

clues.title: Pole: Poletops shaped like upside down trapezoids are common in…
text: Poletops shaped like **upside down trapezoids** are common in central and northern Vietnam.
NOTE: Trapezoidal pole tops may be [off-centre](https://maps.app.goo.gl/hrHUQbXHHTniFB1t9) which is not the same as regular off-centre poles.

clues.title: Pole: The trapezoid shaped poletops can sometimes be off-centre
text: The trapezoid shaped poletops can sometimes be off-centre. If a utility pole has **three off-centre incomplete trapezoids** then you will be in the north of the country.

clues.title: Pole: Poletops shaped like a triangle
text: Poletops shaped like a **triangle**, with the support bars underneath the crossbar, are found in southern Vietnam.
NOTE: The middle insulator must be mounted onto the pole itself, rather than on a [metal extension ](https://maps.app.goo.gl/7tDNw4eb1L7yeHw29)of the crossbar.

clues.title: Pole: A poletop shaped like an A above a crossbar can be found in…
text: A poletop shaped like an **A above a crossbar** can be found in the centre of the country.

clues.title: Pole: Utility poles with uneven crossbars
text: Utility poles with **uneven crossbars**, meaning the crossbar is significantly more to one side of the pole than the other, are found in the south of the country. Sometimes, they are not fully uneven but are more in the style of [Indonesian off-centre poles](https://maps.app.goo.gl/TiDuQt7tSV8UmA3K7).

NOTE: You may mistake partially [off-centre trapezoid](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ieZHLc3qyVbNUXRz5) poletops for regular off-centre poletops, however any pole with a trapezoid connector belongs in a different category. In the exception, the connector is not a straight bar, rather it is an incomplete trapezoid.

clues.title: Pole: Thin bamboo poles can be found in rural areas of the…
text: Thin **bamboo poles** can be found in rural areas of the northwestern mountains.

clues.title: Pole: Poles in the northern parts of the country will often have…
text: Poles in the northern parts of the country will often have **black pole stickers**, similar to those found in Malaysia but often with a more simple design.

clues.title: Shitcam is only found in a few spots in the Red River Delta
text: Shitcam is only found in a few spots in the Red River Delta.

clues.title: The countryside directly around the city of Đà Lạt is…
text: The countryside directly around the city of Đà Lạt is densely covered in **greenhouses**.

clues.title: Landscape: The Đồng Văn Karst Geopark in northern Hà Giang province
text: The Đồng Văn Karst Geopark in northern Hà Giang province, in the extreme northernmost tip of Vietnam, is characterized by a very distinct landscape: **rounded, pointy mountains** with relatively sparse vegetation, exposing the **very dark rocks** underneath.
NOTE: The broader region of northern Vietnam is also characterized by pointy mountains. The Geopark is unique because of the exposed rocks.

clues.title: Google car: The island of Phú Quốc is found in southern Vietnam near…
text: The island of Phú Quốc is found in southern Vietnam near Cambodia. Phú Quốc only has Generation 3 coverage and has a lot of dark red soil. You may sometimes see a large forested ridge, which sits northeast on the island.

clues.title: On the coastal roads of the Hạ Long Bay
text: On the coastal roads of the Hạ Long Bay, east of Hải Phòng, you can see numerous **pointy, rocky islands** rising out of the water, making for idyllic views.

clues.title: Landscape: A single large mountain in the middle of an otherwise…
text: A **single large mountain** in the middle of an otherwise completely flat landscape can be found just northeast of the city of Tây Ninh.

clues.title: This peninsula in far northern Khánh Hoà can be recognised…
text: This peninsula in far northern Khánh Hoà can be recognised by the many **sand dunes** hugging the road, which is mostly a divided highway, but also a [smaller paved road](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Nu1tRXJb6Tq17hYT9) for a shorter stretch.

clues.title: Architecture: The historic town of Hội An
text: The historic town of Hội An, just south of Da Nang, can be recognised by the **old yellow buildings** typically with dark brown doors and details.

clues.title: Landscape: Sa Pa is a resort town deep in the northern mountains…
text: Sa Pa is a resort town deep in the northern mountains overflowing with touristy stores and restaurants with excessive signage, and palace-like grand hotels throughout the town. The architecture is a mixture of an [affluent European style](https://maps.app.goo.gl/fbuKyfSwu2fYfuVb9) and a more typical [southeast Asian style](https://maps.app.goo.gl/YuBdCAmfD2rs74it7).

clues.title: Sign: Near the beach resorts just east of Phan Thiết city
text: Near the beach resorts just east of Phan Thiết city, most signs will have **Cyrillic text** alongside Vietnamese, catering to Russian tourists.

clues.title: Pole: twin poles
text: Like in Czechia and Slovakia, concrete poles attached in pairs are very common and is a good clue for Vietnam.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: mounted spools
text: Mounted spools are spools mounted directly to the pole. In opposition to the mini bars where spools can also be found. It is almost exclusive to the far south of the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: (half) trapezoid support
text: Trapezoid support is where you have a crossbar with a diagonal support attached to a small horizontal segment below. This forms a trapezoid underneath the bar. As you can see in the images, it can be seen on both sides or just one half of it.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: plain round concrete
text: The plain concrete pole has no holes in it. The pole top does not matter and it can also be found doubled up, with two next to each other. Most common in the north.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: cone guard
text: A cone shaped possum guard.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: mini bars
text: Mini bars are super short L shaped crossbars on top of poles. They usually have small spools on top. They are generally found north, but reach quite far south as well.
NOTE: In the north they are usually mounted on holey poles whereas in the central region they are usually mounted on pinhole poles

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: south triangle
text: South triangle is where you can see small metal bars in a triangle shape underneath the crossbar. Important to note is the lack of a horizontal segment in between the two diagonal segments (that would make it a trapezoid). The two supports should touch in the middle.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: central A-top
text: Central A top is where you can see an A standing on the crossbar. It can be centered or off to the side. It is almost exclusively found in central Vietnam.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: one sided top
text: One sided top is where the pole has the crossbar on one side with a single diagonal support beam. It can either be completely on one side or uneven to one side. Important to note that you should not confuse it with trapezoid support which has an extra horizontal segment in the support beam. It is almost exclusively found in the far south.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: ultra tall pole
text: Ultra tall poles are like the name suggests, Ultra tall. It is almost as if they stacked two poles on top of each other, signified by the small brown section 1/3 up the pole. They are mainly found north, but are also rarely found everywhere else.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: triple half trapezium pole support
text: This pole top is just the trapezoid support but stacked on top of each other three times. It overlaps with the trapezoid region, but is exclusive to the far north.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: holey 3/4
text: This holey pole has holes until about 3/4 upwards and is unique to the north. The standard holey pole can be found everywhere.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: offset-mounted lamp
text: This lamp sometimes connected to utility poles is the Offset mounted lamp. It is attached to the pole with two metal bars and is quite far out from the pole. It is found in the south of the country.
NOTE: There are similar looking lamps.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: half holey
text: Holey poles are concrete squared poles with holes going through the pole at the bottom. Holey poles in general are found more commonly north, but there are three distinct variations of this. The half holey pole is found throughout the entire country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: extended/raised pole
text: Extended top is where the top of the pole is extended with something like a metal frame. It is mainly found south, but can rarely be seen everywhere.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: silver band
text: A silver band — it is probably a possum guard. You will find them in the south and rarely in the central regions.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vietnam
text: In Vietnam, phone numbers start with 0, if it starts with 02 it's a regional number with 2X or 2XX defining an area. Numbers are fairly easy to learn, with 24 for Hanoi, 28 for Ho Chi Minh City, area codes increase from north (2OX) to south (29X).

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Sign: Red white sign post
text: Vietnam uses red-and-white striped signposts, and occasionally red-and-yellow ones.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: triangle supports
text: When two supports of the main crossbar of the pole form triangle it should put you south of the country.
There is similar support that looks like trapezoid so make sure it's actually triangle.
Note: I found those poles rarely north but there was always some other clue to know it's not south.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Ventilation electric box
text: Meter Box Designs with trap door style windows plus ventilation slits on the sides are very common in the province of Khanh Hoa. It can be found everywhere in the province from rural villages to coastal areas.
Note: Other regular Meter box designs can be found throughout the whole country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Dalat green houses
text: Greenhouses can be found in Đà Lạt valley.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Plain concrete pole
text: Plain concrete poles without holes or pinholes are almost exclusively found in northern part of the country.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pepper plantations
text: Pepper planations are most commonly found in Dak Nong, Dak Lak, and Gia Lai provinces.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: North canals
text: Low-lying, agricultural plains sometimes accompanied with canals are common around Nam Định and southern Hanoi.
Note: You can also find canals max south of the country but they will have different landscape.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Central A-shape poletop
text: Central A-shaped top is where you can see an A standing on the crossbar. It can be centered or off to the side. It is almost exclusively found in central Vietnam.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Dragonfruit plantations
text: Dragonfruit plantations are most common in Bình Thuận, but can be found all over the south.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: One sided pole top
text: One sided top is where the pole has the crossbar on one side with a single diagonal support beam. It can either be completely on one side or uneven to one side. Important to note that you should not confuse it with trapezoid support which has an extra horizontal segment in the support beam.
It is almost exclusively found in the far south.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Side mounted lamp
text: Lamp mounted to the side of the pole with 2 brackets is only found in the region shown on second image.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Traditional architecture
text: Traditional architecture can mostly be found in the north, but can be seen in Đắk Lắk and Gia Lai. The landscape will generally be flatter in those two areas, which can be a good clue for that area.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: South Canals
text: Canals are very commonly found in the Mekong Delta. Canals can also be found in the north, but the landscape is very different.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Spools pole
